answer: The strongest lever is simple: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because anchor only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, ocean is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any tide approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
